sources.citation: R. Silberzahn, E. L. Uhlmann, D. P. Martin et al., 'Many Analysts, One Data Set: Making Transparent How Variations in Analytic Choices Affect Results', Advances in Methods and Practices in Psychological Science, 1(3), 2018, pp. 337-356.

quotations.text: Twenty-nine teams involving 61 analysts used the same data set to address the same research question: whether soccer referees are more likely to give red cards to dark-skin-toned players than to light-skin-toned players. Analytic approaches varied widely across the teams, and the estimated effect sizes ranged from 0.89 to 2.93
Twenty teams (69%) found a significant positive relationship, p .05, and nine teams (31%) found a nonsignificant relationship. No team reported a significant negative relationship.
there was little evidence that the variability in estimated effect sizes observed across teams was attributable to a subset of analyses that were lower than the others in quality overall

sources.why_it_is_a_neighbour: The nearest published shape of tonight's design: one task, one input, many independent executors, and the spread between them as the measurement. It differs in what varies. There the analysts chose their own analytic approach; here the specification is fixed and only the implementation of it varies, which is a narrower and harsher test.
sources.what_this_session_does_not_claim: No number here is compared to any number there. Twenty-nine teams of humans and four dispatched workers of one automated system are not the same population.

sources.citation: T. Wolter, 'A Comparison Study of Open Source License Crawler', Bachelor thesis, Friedrich-Alexander-Universität Erlangen-Nürnberg, Technische Fakultät, Department Informatik, submitted 13 May 2019. Supervisors: Prof. Dr. Dirk Riehle, M.B.A., Michael Dorner, M.Sc.
sources.licence: CC BY 4.0, stated on the thesis's own licence page

quotations.text: we performed a two phased benchmark with 6 license crawlers and 75 open source projects. Firstly, we determined which of the software tools found the most licenses in a direct competition. Secondly, we evaluated con ict situations in the output of the best performing license crawlers.

A total of 149884 total license hits occurred while scanning with Scancode and FOSSology. Overall, the two license crawler agreed on their result in 124756 of those cases. This amount to a total of 83.24% of all license hits. However, there were a total of 12564 con ict situation.

Scancode had many false posit- ives, marking license hits that were not actually present or had insu cient data. Overall, the positive prediction value was 37.5%. FOSSology on the other hand stayed neutral in a lot of cases. Thus, it's positive prediction value was much higher with 66.66%.

sources.why_it_is_a_neighbour: It is the prior art for 'independently built licence identifiers disagree with each other', and it puts a number on it: two tools, 83.24 % agreement over 149,884 hits. Same author group as Wolter, Barcomb, Riehle & Harutyunyan 2022, which this practice already carries from 2026-09-18.
sources.how_tonight_differs: Those are six tools built to six different purposes by six different projects; the disagreement between them is expected and its causes are many. Tonight holds the specification fixed — one published text, reimplemented — so a disagreement is attributable to the reading of that text and to nothing else.
sources.novelty_position: No novelty of method is claimed. Independent reimplementation is old and comparing licence identifiers is published. What this session has not found published is the subject: an automated research practice's own measuring rule, with three defects already known and disclosed, handed back as a specification to be implemented again.
